lever_choice.chosen: price_plus_reply (price AND reply_rate as one selection rule) run on top of cap volume (5/day)

lever_choice.why: price_plus_reply is the top lever on BOTH deciding cases: base P(G2) 0.737 and pessimistic 0.298 on top of cap volume (mean 0.678) — materially above every alternative. The mechanism: selecting ¥10-15k small-scope requests lifts the average order so ONE order meets G2 (orders_needed 2->1), which removes the binomial penalty of needing two independent wins; being an early applicant (<=3rd-5th) + a free dummy-data sample up front roughly doubles the reply rate. It is a single selection rule, not two separate campaigns, so it costs no extra proposals. Cap volume (5/day well-fit) is the substrate we still maximize, but it is not itself the chosen lever.

not_chosen.volume: LOWEST: base P(G2) 0.2, pessimistic 0.021. Pushing to the 5/day cap alone still leaves orders_needed=2 at the base ¥8k avg, and supply (well-fit requests/day) caps how far volume can go. We do NOT default to the base-case 140 proposals / 14/day — supply cannot deliver it and it is the weakest lever by P(G2).

not_chosen.price: base 0.485, pessimistic 0.162 — strong, but leaving reply at 5% wastes the same selection effort; price_plus_reply dominates it on both cases.
not_chosen.close_rate: base 0.352, pessimistic 0.043 — needs replies first, of which we have 0; closing tactics (sample-before-start, pay-on-acceptance) are adopted anyway but cannot be the primary lever with 0 replies.
